editorial:
Imagine the nerves and excitement of finally getting a surgery you have wanted for years. You follow Matt, a guy who is finally at the hospital for his top surgery. He has his energetic girlfriend, Leisha, right there to keep his spirits up while they deal with all the annoying hospital paperwork. The vibe starts off feeling like a normal day, but it quickly turns into something much deeper. As Matt goes under for the procedure, the movie takes a wild turn. He starts seeing flashes of his younger self, Kimberly, and has to face some old memories he tried to leave behind.

What really makes this work is how it handles the emotional side of things. The acting feels real, especially when Matt deals with the grief of losing his mom, Nancy. The way the story jumps between the past and present is smooth and keeps you interested without being confusing. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the payoff is totally worth it. You should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night. It is a touching story that anyone who loves a good character study will enjoy.
endingExplained: At the end, Matt has a final emotional talk with the memory of his mother. He realizes that letting go of his past as Kimberly does not mean erasing it, but accepting it to move forward. He wakes up from surgery feeling a sense of peace and wholeness. The movie wraps up with Matt and Leisha leaving the hospital, showing that he has finally found the comfort in his own skin he was searching for.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves moving stories about identity and family.
